title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors of DBI and employees, collectively 'Employees' (the defined term includes Directors). Subject to the full policy uniformly except for approval routing and Director-specific reporting.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: The CEO and other Directors of DBI. Distinguished for post-trade confirmation to the Company Secretary and because their approval requests are routed to the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board. Distinguished only in that their approval requests are routed to the Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee rather than the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Employee (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants), and a company or other entity the Employee can control. The Employee must ensure Connected Persons deal only when the Employee would be permitted to, including obtaining clearance on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to ASX of the full-year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to ASX of the half-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time; whether such additional periods are kept confidential is not addressed, though a refusal or revocation of an individual approval must be kept confidential (4.3(c)).

rules.detail: A derivative that operates to limit economic risk (e.g. a collar) is 'hedging' and DBI securities acquired under an equity plan must never be hedged prior to vesting.
rules.evidence: DBI securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by DBI must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Derivatives that hedge economic risk are also banned while the securities are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under an equity plan.
rules.evidence: DBI securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by DBI.

rules.detail: Once vested and unrestricted, entering a derivative is a dealing requiring prior approval under the general section 4 process, outside blackout periods and without Inside Information; the vesting-based hedging ban no longer applies.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 3.3, Employees must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in DBI’s securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging DBI securities acquired under an equity plan prior to vesting.
rules.evidence: DBI securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by DBI must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging while securities remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under an equity plan.
rules.evidence: DBI securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by DBI.

rules.detail: Hedging of fully vested, unrestricted DBI securities is not banned outright; it is a dealing requiring prior approval under section 4, outside blackout periods and without Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation arrangement (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named; it is an agreement to deal caught by the general approval requirement, and if entered within 3 months of another dealing it may separately be caught as short-term dealing (forward contracts are given as an example under 3.4).
rules.evidence: buy or sell securities in a company, or enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

rules.detail: Outright ban on dealing on a speculative basis, including short-selling.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in DBI securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling. Short-selling involves borrowing and selling securities in the hope that they can be bought back at a lower price in the future to close out the short position at a profit.

rules.detail: Lending out one's own securities is not named; only borrowing securities to short-sell is described, as an example of prohibited speculative dealing.
A CFD that limits economic risk of holding DBI securities is 'hedging' and is banned prior to vesting on the same basis as any other hedge.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.

rules.detail: A CFD over fully vested, unrestricted DBI securities is a hedging arrangement permitted subject to the general section 4 approval process.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of DBI securities; no exception process (Board or otherwise) is provided for this restriction.
rules.evidence: Employees are prohibited from entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of DBI securities.

rules.detail: Only 'margin lending arrangements' are named; granting security or a charge over DBI securities outside a margin lending arrangement is not separately addressed, and no carve-out for other secured loans is given.
The policy regulates 'margin lending' by name only; other secured financing arrangements in respect of DBI securities are neither prohibited nor expressly permitted.

Buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering other short term dealings such as forward contracts, is prohibited; selling securities received on vesting within 3 months of the vesting date is excepted.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in DBI’s securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: Requests for approval under 4.1 or 4.2 should be submitted to the Company Secretary, who will forward it to: the Chair of the Board (in the case of the CEO or other Directors) ... Following any trade, Directors must promptly notify the Company Secretary, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into
clearance.evidence: the Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee (in the case of the Chair of the Board)
the CEO (in all other cases). ... Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 3 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval)

clearance.approver: via the Employee, routed under 4.3 to the applicable approver
clearance.evidence: Employees must take appropriate steps to ensure that their “Connected Persons” only deal in securities in circumstances where the Employee to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy, for example, by obtaining clearance in accordance with this Policy in respect of the Connected Persons’ dealings.

carve_outs: Selling securities received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 3 months of the vesting date
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts). Selling securities received on vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 3 months of the vesting date is not a short-term dealing.

exceptions.evidence: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by DBI. However, where securities in DBI granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy
acquisition of DBI securities through a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan
acquisition of DBI securities through a security purchase plan available to all retail securityholders; acquisition of DBI securities through a rights issue
the disposal of DBI securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of DBI securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary)

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board / Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee / CEO, as applicable under 4.3
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board / Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee / CEO, as applicable under 4.3

exemption_authority: The Chair of the Board (for the CEO or other Directors), the Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee (for the Chair of the Board), or the CEO (for all other Employees) may grant approval to deal during a blackout period only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order) accompanied by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action; the approver need not give reasons and may revoke approval at any time, and a refusal or revocation must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: DBI will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar structured to avoid the words 'hedging' or 'margin lending' will still be assessed on its economic substance, so documentation choices are unlikely to avoid the express restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should build in execution risk: approval to deal can be revoked without reasons at any time before the trade completes, and the executive cannot disclose that a refusal or revocation occurred.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban with no carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees are prohibited from entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of DBI securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no Board approval process or exceptional-circumstances carve-out for margin lending, and non-margin secured financing is not separately addressed, so the loan leg sits in an unaddressed grey zone that the Company Secretary should confirm is not caught by this ban before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding DBI securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This definition is broad enough to catch a collar's combined put/call position regardless of how it is documented, so the vesting-state restrictions in 3.6 govern the derivative legs directly.

summary: Over fully vested, unrestricted DBI securities, the put and call legs of a collar are 'hedging' (broadly defined to include any arrangement limiting economic risk) and are not banned outright; they may proceed with prior written approval under the ordinary section 4 process (Chair of the Board, Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee, or the CEO depending on the Employee's role), outside blackout periods and without Inside Information. Hedging of unvested plan securities, or vested securities still subject to a holding lock, is banned absolutely with no exception. The loan leg is more difficult: margin lending arrangements in respect of DBI securities are prohibited outright with no Board or hardship exception anywhere in the policy, and the policy does not separately address non-margin secured financing, leaving a bank loan secured on the collared shares in an unaddressed grey area that would need confirmation from the Company Secretary. Approval to deal, once granted, must be exercised within 3 business days, can be revoked at any time without reasons, and any refusal or revocation must be kept confidential. Overall, the derivative legs look achievable case-by-case on vested, unrestricted shares, but the funded loan leg is either prohibited (if characterised as margin lending) or unaddressed, so bespoke sign-off from DBI would be needed before a funded collar could proceed.
